newsitem.title: GREECE: Natl Bank/Greece profit up 89pct y/y in Jan-May.
newsitem.headline: Natl Bank/Greece profit up 89pct y/y in Jan-May.

text.p: Pretax profits at state National Bank of Greece, the country's largest commercial bank, jumped 89 percent year-on-year to 24.1 billion in the first five months of 1997, its chairman, Theodore Karazas told reporters.
Karatzas was speaking before the bank's annual general shareholders meeting.
"These results came despite additional provisions of 7.0 billion drachmas versus nil in the first five months of 1996," he said.
The bank will continue its 'exceptional course' in the rest of 1997, said Karatzas.
National Bank's pretax profits before provisions rose 14.2 percent to 61.4 billion drachmas in 1996 against 53.8 billion in 1995.
Its consolidated pretax profits before provisions increased 36.4 percent to 127.3 billion drachmas in 1996 from 93.3 billion in 1995.

Its insolvency ratio currently stood between 9.0 and 10 percent and was expected to be above 12 percent after the bank's share capital increase planned for this Fall, making National Bank one of the most powerful in Europe, said Karatzas.
"Competition comes from globalisation and cross-border transactions," said Karatzas who pointed out that the bank's future was abroad. "The bank's growth will be in the periphery."
National Bank of Greece will strengthen its presence in all major financial markets and become a force to reckon with in southeastern Europe, said Karatzas in a recent interview with Reuters.
The bank also decided to offer cheaper working capital loans to its best clients with the floor rate set at 12 percent, he added.
Clients with a good record for a year will be entitled to an interest cut of 100 basis points, said Karatzas.

Clients who take at least 35 percent of their bank loans from the National Bank of Greece will enjoy an additional half a point rate cut and some of them who meet even more criteria will receive an extra rate cut of half a point, he added.
The loan rate cuts will go into effect retroactively, starting June 16, and will be passed on to clients every quarter begining this September. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
